selected_hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat trip to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unforgettable experience. Boat tours depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and include swimming stops in the crystal-clear Ionian Sea.

experiences.name: Santorini Caldera Beach Hopping by Catamaran
experiences.description: Sail along Santorini's dramatic volcanic caldera on a shared catamaran tour visiting Red Beach, White Beach, and the hot springs near Palea Kameni. Enjoy a traditional Greek BBQ lunch on board with local wine, swim in volcanic waters, and soak in breathtaking sunset views from the sea.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club Day at Paradise Beach
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed day at the world-famous Paradise Beach on Mykonos. Rent a sunbed, swim in the clear Aegean waters, and enjoy fresh seafood and Greek mezedes at the beachside tavernas. The lively atmosphere and stunning scenery make it a quintessential Greek island beach experience.

experiences.name: Seaside Greek Cooking Class in Chania
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class steps from the Cretan waterfront in Chania's old town. Learn to prepare traditional Cretan dishes like dakos, spanakopita, fresh grilled octopus, and loukoumades using locally sourced olive oil, herbs, and vegetables. Enjoy your meal with local Cretan wine overlooking the Venetian harbor.

experiences.name: Thessaloniki Waterfront Food & Mezedes Tour
experiences.description: Explore Thessaloniki's legendary food scene along the scenic seaside promenade. Sample bougatsa (custard pastry), fresh grilled sardines, local cheeses, and ouzo-paired mezedes at traditional ouzeries and tavernas along the Thermaic Gulf waterfront. Thessaloniki is widely considered Greece's culinary capital and this tour captures its best flavors.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus or Metro Line 3 to Piraeus Port (budget option ~€6). Board the afternoon/evening ferry to Zakynthos (Zante). Ferry journey takes approximately 6–7 hours — enjoy the Ionian Sea views from the deck.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Zakynthos Town port. Take a local KTEL bus or shared taxi to your accommodation near Navagio Beach area. Check in to the Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a short evening stroll around the nearest village.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) at the airport before or after landing — budget ~€4
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own sandwiches or buy a gyros wrap at Piraeus port for ~€3
meals.dinner: Simple taverna near your accommodation — try grilled sardines and a Greek salad. Budget ~€10–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket from Piraeus to Zakynthos in advance via Ferryhopper or DirectFerries to get the best budget price (~€25–35). Keep all receipts and tickets organized from day one.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and explore the iconic Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach). Access is by boat only — join a shared boat tour from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port (~€15–20 per person). Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the turquoise waters and the famous shipwreck wreck up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Navagio by boat. Head to the nearby Navagio Viewpoint (free, accessible by road) for the most spectacular panoramic photo of the beach from above. Walk along the clifftop trail and enjoy the stunning Ionian Sea vistas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village. Visit a local mini-market to pick up fresh fruit, olives, and local bread for a budget picnic snack. Relax at a nearby small beach or the hotel terrace as the sun sets over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby café — Greek yogurt with honey and a freddo espresso. Budget ~€5
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab a souvlaki wrap from a local kiosk near the port (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner — try moussaka or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) with local house wine. Budget ~€12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and bring water — the 29°C heat is intense on the open boat and clifftop. Navagio boat tours are cheapest when booked locally at the port rather than through hotel desks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a KTEL bus or rent a scooter (~€15/day) to explore the northern Zakynthos coastline. Visit the Blue Caves near Cape Skinari — a natural sea cave system with stunning blue-lit waters. Boat trips into the caves depart from Cape Skinari and cost ~€10–15.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Agios Nikolaos village for a swim at the calm, clear beach there. It's less crowded than the main tourist spots and free to access. Snorkel in the warm Ionian water (sea temp ~24°C) and relax on the pebble shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio area. Explore the local village on foot — browse small shops selling local honey, olive oil, and Zakynthian mandolato (nougat) as affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Home-style breakfast at the boutique stay or a village bakery — spanakopita (spinach pie) and coffee. Budget ~€4–5
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus or calamari at a small fish taverna in Agios Nikolaos village. Budget ~€10
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using local market produce (tomatoes, feta, olives, bread) — budget evening at ~€5 total

day_by_day.notes: Renting a scooter gives you the most freedom to explore northern Zakynthos on a budget. Always wear a helmet and carry your passport as ID. Check if your boutique stay offers free or discounted scooter rental.

day_by_day.morning: Take the KTEL bus to Zakynthos Town (the island's capital). Explore the historic Venetian Castle of Zakynthos (Bochali Hill) — entry is free or ~€3. Enjoy sweeping views over the town and harbor from the hilltop ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Zakynthos Town's main square (Plateia Solomou), visit the Byzantine Museum (~€4 entry) housing rescued post-Byzantine icons and artworks. Stroll along the seafront promenade and browse the local market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the town's backstreets for authentic local dining. Try a traditional kantina (small local eatery) for an affordable sit-down meal before catching the last KTEL bus back to Navagio area.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast in Zakynthos Town at a local café — freddo cappuccino and a koulouri (sesame bread ring). Budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Visit the central market area — pick up fresh local produce, olives, and cheese for a DIY picnic in Plateia Solomou. Budget ~€6
meals.dinner: Traditional psistaria (grill house) in Zakynthos Town — lamb chops or chicken souvlaki with pita and tzatziki. Budget ~€10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses in Zakynthos are very affordable (~€2–4 per trip) but run on limited schedules — check timetables at the bus station or online in advance. The last bus back may be early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Porto Vromi Beach — a stunning hidden cove near Navagio, accessible by a rough road (scooter or 4WD recommended) or short boat ride. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water in a sheltered bay with dramatic cliff scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Porto Vromi or walk the coastal path to discover smaller secluded coves nearby. Bring your own snorkeling gear or rent cheaply from a local water sports shack. The warm sea (24°C) is perfect for extended swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Navagio viewpoint — enjoy a cold Mythos beer or fresh lemonade while watching the golden sunset over the Ionian Sea. Budget ~€4–6 for drinks.

meals.breakfast: Prepare your own breakfast using market supplies — bread, local honey, fruit, and instant coffee. Budget ~€3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic to Porto Vromi — local cheese, olives, tomatoes, and bread. Budget ~€5
meals.dinner: Seafood taverna near the accommodation — fresh grilled fish of the day (ask what's freshest and cheapest) with village salad and house wine. Budget ~€14–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Porto Vromi is also the main departure point for Navagio boat tours, so mornings can get busy with tour boats. Arrive early for the calmest swimming experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Check out of the Navagio boutique stay. Take the ferry from Zakynthos Town back to Killini on the Peloponnese mainland (~1.5 hours, ~€8–10). Then take a bus or train toward Athens or your next Greek destination.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Athens. Check in to a budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood (budget options ~€20–35/night for a private room or dorm). Drop your bags and head out to explore the Monastiraki Flea Market — a vibrant bazaar full of antiques, street food, and local color.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the Acropolis Hill base area and explore the Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district with narrow cobblestone streets, bougainvillea-draped houses, and small tavernas. Enjoy the atmosphere as the city cools down in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — yogurt or a pie from the local bakery. Budget ~€4
meals.lunch: Street food in Monastiraki — a classic gyros pita wrap (pork or chicken) from a street kiosk. Budget ~€3
meals.dinner: Dinner in Psiri or Monastiraki — try a mezze spread (dips, dolmades, fried zucchini) at a traditional ouzeri. Budget ~€12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Athens is a great budget city — most ancient sites are within walking distance of the center. Consider buying the combined ticket for multiple Acropolis-area sites (~€30) which you'll use tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens — arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to beat the heat and the crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. The combined site ticket (~€30) covers multiple nearby sites. The views over Athens are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in combined ticket) — the ancient marketplace and civic center of classical Athens. Visit the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Then explore the New Acropolis Museum (~€5 entry) — one of Greece's finest modern museums.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio or Koukaki neighborhood for a relaxed evening. These residential areas have authentic local tavernas away from the tourist crowds. Watch the sunset over the Acropolis from Filopappou Hill (free, 10-minute walk from Thissio).

meals.breakfast: Café in Monastiraki — Greek coffee and a bougatsa (custard pastry). Budget ~€4–5
meals.lunch: Grab a quick souvlaki or spanakopita from a street kiosk near the Acropolis. Budget ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Local taverna in Koukaki — try pastitsio (Greek lasagna) or lamb kleftiko with a carafe of house wine. Budget ~€12–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Acropolis is extremely hot in the afternoon sun — wear a hat, bring 1.5L of water, and apply sunscreen. Comfortable walking shoes are essential on the uneven ancient stone surfaces.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Athens Metro (Line 1, ~€1.40) to Piraeus and catch an early morning ferry to Hydra Island (~1.5 hours by Flying Dolphin hydrofoil, ~€25–30 return). Hydra is a car-free island with stunning architecture, donkeys as transport, and beautiful harbor scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Hydra's accessible beaches — Vlychos or Kamini are short walks or donkey rides from the port. The crystal-clear Saronic Gulf water is warm and calm. Explore the pretty harbor town with its neoclassical mansions and narrow lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the late afternoon hydrofoil back to Piraeus. Return to Athens by Metro. Spend the evening in the lively Exarchia or Psiri neighborhoods — great for cheap local bars, street art, and authentic Athens nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Piraeus port — a cheese pie and coffee from a port-side bakery. Budget ~€4
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a small taverna on Hydra harbor — grilled sea bream or calamari. Budget ~€12–15
meals.dinner: Budget dinner back in Athens — a classic gyros plate (not wrap) with fries and salad at a local grill house. Budget ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is a day trip gem — no cars, no motorbikes, just donkeys and boats. It's slightly pricier than the mainland but worth the splurge for the unique atmosphere. Book the hydrofoil in advance in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus from Athens' Kifissos Bus Terminal to Nafplio (~2.5 hours, ~€14). Nafplio is one of Greece's most beautiful small cities — the first capital of modern Greece. Check in to a budget guesthouse (~€30–40/night). Explore the charming old town with its Venetian architecture and narrow lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to the magnificent Palamidi Fortress (999 steps or drive up — entry ~€8). The panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf and the old town are breathtaking. Then walk down to Arvanitia Beach — a small rocky beach right below the city walls, free and refreshing for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Nafplio's elegant Syntagma Square and the seafront promenade. Enjoy an evening coffee or ouzo at one of the square's cafés — people-watching at its finest.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the Athens bus terminal before departure — a koulouri and coffee. Budget ~€3
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch in Nafplio old town — try a local gyros or a cheese-filled pie from a bakery. Budget ~€5–6
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner in Nafplio — fresh Argolic Gulf seafood, stuffed peppers, and local Nemea wine. Budget ~€13–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is a wonderful change of pace from Athens — quieter, more romantic, and deeply historical. The Palamidi climb is strenuous in the heat — go in the late afternoon when it's cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short taxi or bus from Nafplio to Epidaurus (~30 minutes, ~€15 by taxi or ~€3 by bus). Visit the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world, famous for its extraordinary acoustics. Entry ~€12. Test the acoustics yourself by standing in the center and whispering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and head to Tolo Beach (~20 minutes by local bus, ~€2) — a long sandy beach on the Argolic Gulf with calm, warm water. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Beach is free with sunbeds available for rent (~€5–8 for two).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nafplio for a final evening in this beautiful town. Explore the Bourtzi Castle on the small island in the harbor (accessible by boat, ~€5 return). Watch the sunset from the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Nafplio café — Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts, plus coffee. Budget ~€5–6
meals.lunch: Picnic at Tolo Beach — pick up supplies from a Nafplio mini-market (bread, local cheese, tomatoes, olives). Budget ~€6
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a nice Nafplio taverna — fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine shared between two. Budget ~€16–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: If visiting Epidaurus, check if there's an evening performance at the ancient theatre — the summer festival (June–August) hosts Greek drama performances which are an unforgettable experience (~€15–25 tickets).

day_by_day.morning: Take the KTEL bus back to Athens (~2.5 hours). From Athens, take the Metro to Piraeus and catch a ferry to Aegina Island (~1 hour, ~€8–10 each way) — the closest Saronic island to Athens and very budget-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: In Aegina, rent a bicycle (~€8/day) to explore the island. Visit the stunning Temple of Aphaia (~€6 entry) — a remarkably well-preserved ancient Greek temple with panoramic sea views. Then cycle down to Agia Marina Beach — the island's best sandy beach with warm, calm water for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the late ferry back to Piraeus. Return to Athens for your final nights. Spend the evening in the Thissio neighborhood — great rooftop bars with Acropolis views for a sundowner drink.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Athens bus terminal or a nearby café before heading to Piraeus. Budget ~€4
meals.lunch: Aegina's famous pistachios and a fresh fish lunch at the harbor — the island is renowned for its pistachio production. Budget ~€10–12
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — try a traditional ouzeri in Thissio with a selection of mezze plates and ouzo. Budget ~€12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Aegina pistachios are a must-try and make excellent budget souvenirs — buy them directly from roadside stalls or the port market for the best prices. Much cheaper than tourist shops.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Athens' Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a vibrant, authentic covered market with meat, fish, spice, and produce stalls. A fascinating cultural experience and great for picking up local food souvenirs (olive oil, herbs, honey). Then visit the nearby Omonia Square area — the real working-class heart of Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (~€12 entry) — one of the world's greatest collections of ancient Greek art and artifacts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the incredible collection of sculptures, pottery, and gold artifacts. Then relax in the Pedion tou Areos park nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — head to the Monastiraki area for a farewell dinner. Walk through the lively Adrianou Street and enjoy the buzzing atmosphere. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the end of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Monastiraki — a proper Greek café breakfast with eggs, feta, olives, and coffee. Budget ~€7–8
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the National Museum — souvlaki wrap and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget ~€5
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Monastiraki — a full Greek mezze feast with dips, grilled meats, saganaki (fried cheese), and wine. Budget ~€15–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. The museum is large; wear comfortable shoes and allow at least 2.5 hours to see the highlights without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Wake up early for a last Greek coffee and pastry at a neighborhood café. Take a final walk through Plaka and Anafiotika — the tiny Cycladic-style neighborhood built into the Acropolis rock, quiet and magical in the early morning before the tourist crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head to the airport via Metro Line 3 from Syntagma or Monastiraki (~35 minutes, ~€9). Check in, clear security, and enjoy a final Greek coffee or a last bite of baklava at the airport before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — fly home with memories of turquoise Ionian waters, ancient ruins, fresh seafood, and the warm hospitality of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a proper freddo espresso and a fresh loukoumades (honey doughnuts) from a street stall. Budget ~€4–5
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a final gyros wrap near the hotel before checkout. Budget ~€5–7
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snack depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Metro journey and airport check-in/security. Athens airport is efficient but can get busy in peak summer season. Keep €9 in coins or card for the Metro ticket to the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Navagio Beach boutique hotel (approx. 1.5–2 hrs including ferry crossing to Zakynthos). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the local area near your accommodation to get oriented. Enjoy the stunning coastal scenery around Navagio.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby taverna in the Anafonitria village area for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the quiet surroundings and enjoy the warm evening air with a glass of local Verdea wine.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light bite at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a café near the port or on the ferry during transfer
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or a local village taverna in Anafonitria — try grilled octopus and Greek salad (approx. €20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — travel fatigue is real. Prioritize settling in and hydrating. The ferry crossing from the mainland or inter-island transfer can be scenic and enjoyable.

day_by_day.morning: Morning tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon in Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch and a walk through the Plaka district in Athens.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Temple of Olympian Zeus in Athens, then back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel — enjoy local yogurt with thyme honey, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Pack a light picnic or grab snacks from a local shop before the boat trip — enjoy on the boat
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Volimes village — try lamb kleftiko and tzatziki (approx. €18–25 per person)

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or car and drive south to the Marathonisi Turtle Island area near Laganas Bay. Take a short boat ride to Marathonisi to see loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) nesting on the beach — a truly magical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Gerakas Beach on the southeastern tip of the island, one of Zakynthos's most beautiful and protected beaches. Swim and sunbathe on the golden sand. The beach is a protected nesting site so follow posted rules.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) for the evening. Walk along the waterfront promenade, visit Solomos Square, and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside café near Gerakas — grilled fish of the day and a cold Mythos beer (approx. €15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zakynthos Town at a harbourfront restaurant — try fresh grilled sea bream and local Zakynthian pasta (approx. €22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is recommended for this day — approx. €35–50/day. Gerakas Beach has restricted access after sunset to protect turtle nests. Return to hotel by evening.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at a quieter beach near your hotel — Porto Vromi cove is ideal. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the scenery. The calm morning waters are perfect for snorkeling around the rocky edges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Byzantine Museum and Solomos Museum in Zakynthos Town to learn about the island's rich cultural heritage, including its role in Greek literature and the devastating 1953 earthquake reconstruction.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kantada music performance if available locally (check with your hotel), or enjoy a relaxed evening at a wine bar in Zakynthos Town sampling local Verdea white wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap and fresh lemonade from a local street food stall in Zakynthos Town (approx. €8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Mezedes dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Zakynthos Town — share multiple small plates including dolmades, saganaki, and taramasalata (approx. €20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Museum entry fees are typically €3–6 each. A relaxed cultural afternoon balances the beach-heavy days nicely.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (approx. 1.5 hrs). Arrive at Poros or Argostoli and check into a mid-range hotel or guesthouse. Drop your bags and head to Myrtos Beach — one of the most photographed beaches in Greece — for a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Melissani Cave Lake near Sami — an otherworldly underground lake where sunlight pierces through a collapsed ceiling and illuminates the water in brilliant blue and turquoise hues. Take the short boat ride inside the cave.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Argostoli town for the evening. Walk along the waterfront and watch loggerhead turtles that often gather near the fishing harbor at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before ferry departure — coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery
meals.lunch: Picnic supplies from a local market near Myrtos Beach or a simple beachside snack bar
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at a harbourfront taverna in Argostoli — try Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) and local Robola wine (approx. €22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets should be booked in advance. Melissani Cave entry is approx. €7. Myrtos Beach has limited shade — bring an umbrella and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Antisamos Beach near Sami — a stunning pebble beach with incredibly clear water, famously used as a filming location. Swim and relax in the morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic village of Assos perched on a small peninsula with a Venetian castle above. Wander the colorful village streets, swim in the small cove, and hike up to the castle ruins for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Argostoli for dinner. Explore the local market street and try a traditional Kefalonian pastry from a local bakery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kefalonia accommodation
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna in Assos village — try fresh pasta with local cheese and a Greek salad (approx. €15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant in Argostoli — try Kefalonian lamb with pasta and a carafe of house wine (approx. €20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car on Kefalonia is highly recommended — the island is large and public transport is limited. Approx. €40–55/day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fiskardo, the only village on Kefalonia that survived the 1953 earthquake, retaining its original Venetian architecture. Stroll the charming harbor lined with colorful boats and pastel buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Emblisi Beach just outside Fiskardo — a secluded pebble cove with crystal-clear water. Snorkel along the rocky edges. Alternatively, kayak around the Fiskardo peninsula (kayak rental available locally).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner in Fiskardo harbor — one of the most atmospheric dining spots in the Ionian Islands.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation in Argostoli
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Fiskardo — fresh bruschetta, olives, and local cheese (approx. €12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a harbourside restaurant in Fiskardo — grilled lobster pasta or fresh catch of the day (approx. €28–38 per person — a slight splurge for the atmosphere)

day_by_day.notes: Fiskardo is about 50 km from Argostoli — a scenic 1-hour drive through mountains. Consider staying overnight in Fiskardo to enjoy the evening atmosphere without a long drive back.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Kefalonia to Lefkada via Ithaca (or direct depending on schedule). Arrive in Lefkada and check into accommodation. Head straight to Nikiana Beach or Agios Ioannis Beach for a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lefkada Town — a charming town built largely from wood and metal to withstand earthquakes, giving it a unique architectural character. Walk across the causeway, visit the old fortress of Santa Maura, and browse the main pedestrian street.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in Lefkada Town. The main square and waterfront come alive at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before ferry departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Lefkada Town after arrival — try spanakopita and a cold frappe (approx. €10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a taverna near the waterfront in Lefkada Town — try fresh grilled sardines and horiatiki salad (approx. €18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules between Ionian islands vary — confirm times in advance. Lefkada is connected to the mainland by a causeway, making it uniquely accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Porto Katsiki Beach — consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. The dramatic white cliffs plunging into deep blue water are breathtaking. Arrive early for the best experience before it gets crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Egremni Beach nearby — another stunning cliff-backed beach accessible by stairs. Swim and relax. In the late afternoon, drive to Vasiliki village on the southern coast, a windsurfing hub with a lovely harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Vasiliki village watching windsurfers return to shore as the sun sets over the bay.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lefkada accommodation
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Porto Katsiki or packed lunch — fresh sandwiches and fruit
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a taverna in Vasiliki harbor — try grilled calamari and moussaka (approx. €18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki has a small entrance fee for parking (approx. €3–5). The stairs to Egremni Beach are steep — wear good footwear. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the beautiful village of Nydri on the east coast of Lefkada. Take a boat trip to the nearby small islands of Meganisi, Skorpios (Onassis island), and Sparti — a classic Ionian island-hopping experience with swimming stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nydri and relax on the beach. Browse the waterfront shops and pick up local olive oil, honey, or ceramic souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lefkada Town for a final evening on the island. Enjoy a leisurely dinner and evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation
meals.lunch: Lunch on the boat trip or at a taverna in Nydri — fresh fish and Greek salad (approx. €15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Lefkada Town — try gemista (stuffed tomatoes and peppers) and a local white wine (approx. €18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips from Nydri typically cost €15–25 per person and run most of the day. Book at the harbor in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Drive across the Lefkada causeway to the mainland and head toward Parga — a picturesque coastal town in Epirus (approx. 2.5 hrs drive). Check in and explore the charming Venetian castle overlooking the town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Valtos Beach — a gorgeous sandy beach just a short boat ride or walk from Parga town. Swim and snorkel in the clear Ionian waters.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Parga's narrow, bougainvillea-draped streets and enjoy a sunset drink from a clifftop bar overlooking the castle and islands.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Lefkada accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside taverna at Valtos Beach — grilled fish and tzatziki (approx. €18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Parga town center — try local bourdeto (spicy fish stew) and fresh bread (approx. €20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parga is a hidden gem — less touristy than the islands. A rental car is essential for this day. Alternatively, take a bus from Lefkada to Preveza then onward to Parga.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient Oracle of Dodona (approx. 1.5 hrs inland from Parga) — one of the oldest oracles in ancient Greece, with a well-preserved ancient theater set against a dramatic mountain backdrop. A fascinating and uncrowded historical site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the coast and spend the afternoon at Sarakiniko Beach near Parga — a secluded cove with calm, clear water. Alternatively, take a boat trip to the Paxos and Antipaxos islands for spectacular Blue Caves and beaches (day trip boats available from Parga harbor).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Parga — enjoy a long, leisurely dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip. Toast the journey with a bottle of local wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Parga accommodation — Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or taverna near Dodona — simple mezedes and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner in Parga — splurge slightly on a full mezedes spread with local wine (approx. €28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dodona entry fee is approx. €6. The Paxos day trip is highly recommended if skipping Dodona — it's one of the most beautiful excursions in the Ionian. Book boat trips at Parga harbor the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a slow breakfast and a last walk through Parga or along the beach. Pick up any final souvenirs — local olive oil, thyme honey, or Ionian sea salt make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin transfer toward your departure point. If flying from Preveza/Aktion Airport, it's approx. 45 min from Parga. If flying from Athens, allow 5–6 hrs including a connecting flight or long drive. Enjoy the scenic coastal drive.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home memories of turquoise waters, fresh seafood, warm evenings, and the laid-back rhythm of the Ionian Islands.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at the hotel — pastries, cheese, olives, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the airport or en route — souvlaki or a cheese pie
meals.dinner: Airport dining or onboard flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for car return if renting. Confirm your departure airport when booking — Preveza (PVK) serves the Epirus/Ionian region well. Check in online the night before to save time.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from the airport to your boutique stay at Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island via luxury chauffeur-driven vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique hotel and settle in. Enjoy a welcome drink on your private terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea. Take a leisurely first stroll along the clifftops above Navagio Beach to soak in the iconic shipwreck panorama at golden-hour light.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle orientation walk through the nearest village. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a highly regarded local taverna specialising in fresh Zakynthian seafood and locally pressed olive oil dishes.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Light snack or mezze platter arranged by the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local seafood taverna — grilled sea bream, octopus carpaccio, local white wine from the Verdea grape variety

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request an early check-in if possible to maximise the afternoon. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion to Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — accessible only by sea. Arrive early before the crowds, swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water beside the famous MV Panagiotis wreck, and enjoy champagne on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour along the dramatic limestone cliffs of the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos. Snorkel in the iridescent blue water inside the sea caves, then anchor in a secluded cove for a gourmet lunch served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Sunset cocktails on the clifftop terrace. Fine dining at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring a tasting menu of modern Greek cuisine with local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, yoghurt, feta, seasonal fruit, freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served on the private boat — charcuterie, local cheeses, seafood salad, chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Hotel signature tasting menu — lobster pasta, slow-roasted lamb with herbs, baklava with pistachio ice cream, paired with premium Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat well in advance. Bring high-SPF sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe sunscreen for the caves. Start early (around 08:00) to reach Navagio before tourist boats arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Zakynthos Town (Zante Town). Visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians, the Byzantine Museum with its extraordinary post-Byzantine icon collection, and the elegant Venetian-influenced Solomos Square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local market and delicatessens of Zakynthos Town. Purchase premium local products — Zakynthian mandolato nougat, local olive oil, and sun-dried figs. Visit a traditional olive oil producer for a private tasting and tour of the press.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Zakynthos Town's finest restaurants on the harbour front, with views over the marina. Try traditional Zakynthian dishes such as sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce) and skordalia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs prepared to order, smoked salmon, Greek yoghurt with local thyme honey
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined harbour-side restaurant in Zakynthos Town — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad with Zakynthian capers, local bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: Upscale restaurant in Zakynthos Town — sofrito, moussaka reimagined with premium ingredients, local Verdea wine

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the day for comfort. The Byzantine Museum is a must — its collection survived the 1953 earthquake and is exceptional. Most shops close for an afternoon siesta between 14:00–17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the clifftop terrace arranged by the hotel. Followed by a slow, indulgent breakfast. Mid-morning, visit the Venetian Castle (Kastro) above Zakynthos Town for sweeping island panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to the Keri Caves and Keri Lighthouse at the southern tip of Zakynthos. Enjoy a private boat trip into the sea caves and swim in secluded bays accessible only by water. Spot loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Return north. Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar with panoramic Ionian Sea views. Dinner at a romantic, candlelit restaurant specialising in wood-fired meats and locally caught fish.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — full spread with pastries, cold cuts, eggs, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a small family-run taverna near Keri village — fried calamari, grilled prawns, village salad
meals.dinner: Romantic clifftop restaurant — wood-fired whole fish, lamb chops with rosemary, local dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: The Caretta caretta sea turtle is a protected species — maintain respectful distance and follow guide instructions. Keri Lighthouse area is particularly photogenic at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at leisure at Navagio Beach area. Private access to a secluded beach cove arranged by the hotel. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe with a personal beach butler service — chilled towels, fresh fruit, and cold drinks provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a local Zakynthian chef at a traditional farmhouse. Learn to prepare authentic island dishes — handmade pasta with lobster, slow-cooked lamb stifado, and traditional loukoumades (honey doughnuts).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you prepared together as a private dinner in the farmhouse garden, under olive trees with local wine and candlelight.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast — yoghurt, fruit, pastries, coffee
meals.lunch: Beach butler service — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit platters, chilled water and juices
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations — lobster pasta, lamb stifado, loukoumades with local thyme honey

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highlight experience — book in advance and request a market visit add-on in the morning if desired. The farmhouse setting is magical at dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Zakynthos by private speedboat or ferry to Kefalonia (approximately 1–1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury hotel in the Fiskardo or Argostoli area. First exploration of the charming Venetian harbour village of Fiskardo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Melissani Cave — a breathtaking underground lake where sunlight pierces the collapsed roof and illuminates the water in vivid blues and greens. Follow with a swim at Antisamos Beach, one of Greece's most beautiful pebble beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Fiskardo village, widely regarded as the most elegant and well-preserved village in the Ionian Islands, with excellent upscale restaurants lining the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — full spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbour-side restaurant in Fiskardo — freshly caught fish, local Robola white wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a Fiskardo harbour restaurant — lobster, premium seafood platter, Kefalonian meat pie as a starter

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat transfer from Zakynthos to Fiskardo is the most scenic and comfortable option. Alternatively, ferry to Sami and then private transfer to Fiskardo. Pre-book Melissani Cave entry — queues can be long in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Kefalonia's highlights — visit Assos, a stunning peninsula village with a 16th-century Venetian fortress. Walk the pine-forested path to the castle ruins for extraordinary views over the turquoise bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Myrtos Beach — arguably one of the most spectacular beaches in all of Greece, with dramatic white pebbles and vivid blue water framed by towering limestone cliffs. Private beach setup with sunbeds and parasols arranged in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo. Sunset drinks on a private yacht or sailboat chartered for the evening, watching the sun dip into the Ionian Sea. Dinner back in the village.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — eggs, pastries, local honey, fresh fruit, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Myrtos Beach — gourmet hamper prepared by the hotel with local cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated Fiskardo restaurant — grilled octopus, sea bass with capers and lemon, local Robola wine

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has no facilities — arrange everything in advance through the hotel. The road down to Myrtos is steep and winding; a 4WD or private driver is recommended. Assos village is best visited before midday to avoid heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Drogarati Cave near Sami — a stunning stalactite and stalagmite cave with remarkable acoustics. Explore at a leisurely pace with a private guide. Afterward, visit the coastal town of Sami and its waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive through the Kefalonian countryside — vineyards, olive groves, and mountain villages. Stop at a local winery for a private tasting of Robola, Kefalonia's prized indigenous white wine variety, with a tour of the cellars.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Kefalonia at a premium restaurant in Argostoli — the island's lively capital, with a beautiful waterfront promenade and excellent dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional village taverna in the mountains — slow-cooked goat, village bread, local salad
meals.dinner: Upscale restaurant in Argostoli — Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), fresh fish, local wine, traditional desserts

day_by_day.notes: Robola wine is unique to Kefalonia and highly regarded — the cooperative winery near Omala is excellent and offers private tastings. Book ahead. Drogarati Cave maintains a cool temperature inside — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer and ferry from Kefalonia to Lefkada (approximately 2 hours by ferry to Nydri or private speedboat). Check in to a luxury villa or boutique hotel near Porto Katsiki or Vasiliki. First impressions of Lefkada's dramatic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porto Katsiki Beach — one of the most iconic beaches in Greece, with sheer white cliffs plunging into impossibly blue water. Arrive by private boat for the best experience and least crowds. Swim and snorkel in pristine conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lefkada Town — a charming, earthquake-resistant town with colourful tin-clad buildings and a vibrant waterfront. Dinner at a premium restaurant overlooking the lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the private boat en route or at a small taverna near Porto Katsiki
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner in Lefkada Town — grilled fish, shrimp saganaki, local feta, regional wine

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki is best accessed by boat — the steps down from the clifftop are steep and crowded in peak season. A private boat approach is the premium option. Lefkada is connected to the mainland by a floating bridge — no ferry needed from the mainland side.

day_by_day.morning: Private sailing excursion from Vasiliki (one of Europe's top windsurfing spots) to the secluded beaches of the south — Egremni Beach, Agiofylli, and the sea caves of Cape Lefkatas. Swim in crystal waters far from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at a secluded cove for an on-board gourmet lunch. Afternoon snorkelling and paddleboarding in calm Ionian waters. The skipper will guide you to the most pristine spots.
day_by_day.evening: Return to harbour at sunset. Freshen up at the hotel. Dinner at a waterfront restaurant in Vasiliki or Nydri, with fresh catch of the day.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — extended, leisurely start
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board lunch prepared by a private chef or catered hamper — fresh seafood, Greek salads, chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant — whole grilled fish, seafood pasta, local dessert

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private sailing charter should be booked well in advance. Vasiliki is renowned for its afternoon thermal winds — sailing conditions are excellent. Apply sunscreen regularly as UV exposure on water is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the hotel pool or private beach. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking along the Lefkada coastline arranged by the hotel. Mid-morning visit to a local olive oil producer for a private estate tour and tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the inland villages of Lefkada — Karya village is famous for its lace embroidery and traditional crafts. Visit the local folklore museum and browse artisan shops. Stop at a traditional kafeneion (coffee house) for Greek coffee and loukoumades.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for a sunset beach experience. Private dinner on the beach — a specially arranged table on the sand with torchlight, fresh seafood, and chilled wine.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast — yoghurt, fruit, pastries
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Karya village — grilled meats, village salad, local bread, carafe of house wine
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner arranged by the hotel — lobster, grilled vegetables, local wine, dessert under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner is a signature luxury experience — arrange at least 48 hours in advance with the hotel concierge. Karya village is best in the afternoon when the heat subsides slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — return by private transfer or speedboat to Zakynthos for one last night, or remain in Lefkada depending on flight logistics. If returning to Zakynthos: check in and spend the morning revisiting favourite spots — perhaps a final swim at Navagio Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulgent spa afternoon at the hotel — traditional Greek massage with olive oil, body scrub, and relaxation treatments. Alternatively, a final private boat trip to a secluded cove for swimming and snorkelling.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the finest restaurant available — a celebration of 13 days of Greek island life. Order the best of everything: fresh lobster, premium Greek wines, and traditional desserts.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — the complete spread, savoured slowly
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a beachside spot — dips, grilled halloumi, fresh bread, cold beer or rosé
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner — lobster, premium cut grilled meats, selection of Greek wines, dessert platter with local spirits

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to purchase any remaining gifts or local products — olive oil, local wine, honey, and ceramics make excellent souvenirs. Confirm departure logistics and transfer times for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last swim or clifftop walk to take in the views one final time. Pack and prepare for departure. Private chauffeur transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Greece. Airport lounge access recommended for a comfortable departure experience.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Greek islands.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — full Greek spread, specialty coffee, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or light meal before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon return home

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the transfer to the airport — island roads can be slow. Request a late checkout from the hotel if your flight departs in the afternoon. Ensure all local purchases are packed securely, especially olive oil and wine bottles.
